What it does (Effect on Model): The most important parameter for PRPD. Because 95% of PRPD is blank background, this forces the Student CNN to ignore the easy "blank" pixels and only backpropagate the top 0.1% worst errors (the actual pulses). Lowering this makes the model lazier; it will just memorize the empty background.
Controls how much temporal (time) context the CNN sees at once. Increasing the width to 512 allows the model to see longer pulse chains, but it exponentially increases GPU VRAM usage.

How many images the CNN processes simultaneously before updating weights. Because we are constrained by the 11GB VRAM of the RTX 2080 Ti, we must keep this at 4 or lower to prevent Out-Of-Memory (OOM) crashes.
The speed at which the Adam optimizer updates the weights. A lower learning rate makes training slower but more stable, preventing the Student from rapidly overshooting the Teacher's feature map.
A regularization penalty applied to the optimizer. It strictly prevents the Student CNN from growing its weights too large, ensuring it doesn't overfit to the small training dataset.

Total passes over the dataset. Because the Student is simply mimicking a frozen Teacher (Distillation), it converges incredibly fast. Training past 10 epochs on small PRPD datasets is usually unnecessary and risks overfitting.

The multiplier that balances the Local Loss (L_ST) against the Global Autoencoder Loss (L_STAE). Increasing this forces the Student to care more about the overall "global structure" (Autoencoder) rather than exact local textures (Teacher).

The depth of the Teacher and Student Patch Description Networks (PDN). Currently set to 4 Conv2D layers (128 -> 256 -> 256 -> 384 channels). Adding more layers allows the network to learn more complex topological shapes but requires much more data to train without overfitting.

The bottleneck mathematically forces the Autoencoder to compress the data, destroying local high-resolution textures so it can only memorize the global structure. Increasing this to 128 allows it to retain more detail, which can sometimes reduce false alarms but risks making it lazier at finding true anomalies.

The Autoencoder currently uses 4 Encoder Conv2D layers and 3 Decoder Conv2D layers. Changing this depth affects how aggressively the network compresses and decompresses the input tensor's spatial dimensions.
